The resulting model achieves 81.64\% success on LIBERO-Plus without additional embodied pretraining data or foundation models, reaches 93.0\% average success on RoboTwin 2.0, and improves real-world manipulation performance.

nominations.title: From Failures to Learnable Worlds: Policy-Conditioned Environment Generation for Navigation Agents
nominations.authors: Yue Zhang, Han Lin, Zun Wang, Yidong Huang, Zaid Khan, Mohit Bansal
nominations.abstract: Simulated environments enable scalable training data generation for embodied agents, but more data does not necessarily provide what a particular agent needs to learn. Existing environment-generation pipelines largely optimize generic properties such as realism, diversity, or task coverage, while different pretrained policies can fail for different environmental reasons. We therefore introduce WEDGE, a framework for weakness-guided navigation learning in which the failure modes of a pretrained agent guide the generation of training environments at each adaptation round. Given a pretrained policy, WEDGE uses an LLM to propose executable weakness features from contrasting successful and failed rollouts, automatically validates them on the diagnostic set, and selects the strongest validated weakness based on its success-rate gap. The validated weaknesses are then mapped to the environmental factors that control them. WEDGE varies these factors to construct environments in the difficulty regimes where the policy struggles, producing targeted training experience for adaptation. Across three navigation agents with different adaptation mechanisms, we find that policies exhibit distinct weakness profiles and benefit from different training environments. Weakness-conditioned adaptation consistently outperforms matched random and hard-example alternatives on ProcTHOR, while the resulting gains for Uni-NaVid and Gemini also extend to HM3D after ProcTHOR adaptation. Iterative re-diagnosis further shows that dominant weaknesses can persist or shift as the policy improves, providing updated guidance for subsequent environment construction. Together, these results show that policy failures are not only diagnostic signals, but actionable guidance for constructing training environments that target a policy's current weaknesses.

nominations.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
nominations.authors: Yingfa Chen, Xingyu Shen, Chaojun Xiao, Xu Han
nominations.abstract: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions. We introduce **Latent Compaction**, which learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training. We initialize cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity. Training first fits attention outputs and log-normalizers to those of the full cache, with reconstruction-selected entries held fixed. It then jointly optimizes the entire cache through end-to-end distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights remain frozen throughout, and training uses only generic prompts about the document, without access to downstream questions or answers. Experiments on RULER, LongBench, and Phonebook Lookup demonstrate substantial gains over budget-matched compression baselines. On a RULER, for example, our method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32times compression, compared with 40.0% for KVZip+. The method also transfers across model scales and families, with retrieval gains on both Qwen3 and MiniCPM5. These results show that treating the KV cache as a neural network and optimizing it with test-time training can preserve retrieval accuracy under aggressive compression. The code is released at https://www.github.com/THUNLP/latent-compaction

nominations.title: SWEeper-Bench: Can Agents Discover Bugs in Interactive Software?
nominations.authors: Yang Yao, Haozhe Chen, Bingyi Kang, Karthik R Narasimhan, Zhuang Liu
nominations.abstract: Coding agents increasingly interact with users by generating interactive software on the fly rather than replying in text, yet many bugs in such software reveal themselves only after multi-step interactions. Today, users must discover these bugs and wait for fixes, making the development loop slow and expensive. Existing benchmarks typically assume the bugs have already been identified, leaving agents' ability to find interaction-dependent failures largely unevaluated. We introduce SWEeper-Bench, 200 tasks built from real bug fixes in 200 widely used open-source web applications. Each task gives the agent only the codebase and an open-ended request such as "Find and fix issues in Focalboard's board sharing and membership." Because these bugs are hard to detect from code alone, agents must design interactive tests to uncover them. An agentic verifier then judges each repair by what a user would observe in the browser. The best of 15 frontier agents passes only 59.0% of tasks. Through stage-by-stage analysis of agent trajectories, we show that the biggest bottleneck is identifying the buggy behavior: agents often reach the relevant feature but never trigger the failure or fail to recognize it. SWEeper-Bench measures progress toward agents that close this loop themselves, delivering software that works without waiting for user feedback.

nominations.title: Diff Diffusion: Predicting Edit Paths with Diffusion Models for Efficient Code Editing
nominations.authors: Xiaolong Xu, Hao Jiang, Bo Jiang, Zhiwen Deng, Ningyuan Sun, Bingzhou Chen, Jin Chen, Chenxing Wei
nominations.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) are appealing for code generation because they can update many tokens in parallel, yet many are optimized for sequence synthesis rather than edit prediction. This setting is poorly matched to modern AI-assisted IDEs, where edit prediction must infer the next code change from recent edits, the current file, and cursor-local context. Such changes are usually sparse and preserve most source tokens, so regenerating a full code segment wastes computation. We propose Diff Diffusion, a diffusion-inspired LLM framework for code editing that predicts edit paths from an original snippet to its revised form. Diff Diffusion represents denoising as structured edit operations, and combines this formulation with multi-stage training and efficient parallel decoding. By focusing computation on changed regions, Diff Diffusion supports accurate low-latency edits and multi-position parallel modification. Across public edit-completion benchmarks, edit-prediction evaluations, and online validation, Diff Diffusion matches or leads autoregressive baselines while delivering 2.78 times faster inference on public edit-completion benchmarks and a 39.0% P50 model-latency reduction in production. This work provides a new modeling perspective for AI applications that require high accuracy and low latency.

nominations.title: The LR2 Lifetime Distribution: Rate Crossing, Reliability Properties, and Estimation
nominations.authors: Lalita Singh
nominations.abstract: We study the LR2 one-parameter lifetime distribution obtained by mixing an exponential component of rate $\theta/2$ and a gamma component with shape four and rate $\theta^2$. The exponential mixing probability is $\theta^2/(1+\theta^2)$ for $\theta>0$. We derive the density, survival function, moments, transforms, truncated moments, quantiles, order-statistic distributions, mean residual life, and stress--strength reliability. Identifiability follows from the density at the origin, and strict monotonicity of the mean yields a unique moment estimator. A complete density-turning-point criterion and analytic initial and tail hazard expansions clarify the possible shapes. The component rates cross at one half. The hazard decreases initially for every positive parameter and eventually increases in the gamma-dominated regime; it eventually decreases in the exponential-dominated regime. We develop likelihood estimation, observed information, constrained expectation--maximization, spacing estimation, and inference under regularity conditions, and state the likelihood for independent right censoring. A reproducible Monte Carlo study with eight settings and 4,000 generated samples compares likelihood and moment estimation and evaluates log-scale confidence intervals. The analysis distinguishes mathematical properties from empirical validation and explains the restrictions associated with a fixed working time unit.

nominations.title: Linear regression with probabilistic networks for network-linked data
nominations.authors: Jingnan Zhang, Shiwen Ye, Danyang Huang
nominations.abstract: Network-linked data combine a network with covariates and responses observed for its nodes. Common regression approaches either model dependence among neighboring responses using the observed network or capture similarities associated with network structure without explicitly modeling response dependence. We propose a probabilistic network-linked data analysis framework that incorporates both features while accounting for randomness in network formation. The model uses normalized connection probabilities to weight peer responses and latent positions to capture network cohesion. A two-step likelihood procedure first estimates the network structure and then fits the response model. We establish theoretical guarantees for network recovery in sparse networks with heterogeneous node effects, and prove consistency and joint asymptotic normality of the regression estimators subject to suitable conditions. The analysis also clarifies when estimating the network preserves the classical convergence rate for spatial autoregressive models. Simulation studies demonstrate the estimation performance of the method and assess its inference accuracy. An analysis of diplomatic network data illustrates its practical application.

nominations.title: Subdata Selection for Measurement-Constrained Linear Regression under Model Misspecification
nominations.authors: Yundi Kong, Min Yang, Ping-Shou Zhong
nominations.abstract: In many modern applications, obtaining response variables is costly, time-consuming, or technically challenging, making it impractical to measure outcomes for all available units. In such settings, covariates may be available for a large pool of candidates, but responses can only be collected for a small, carefully selected subset, making the choice of which units to measure a consequential decision. Most existing subsampling methods are developed for massive datasets, emphasizing the trade-off between statistical accuracy and computational cost, and typically relying on the assumption of a correctly specified model. These features limit their suitability in measurement-constrained settings, where statistical efficiency is paramount and model misspecification is often unavoidable. To address these challenges, we develop a new subset selection framework for linear regression that accommodates potential model misspecification. The proposed approach targets predictive expected loss and yields an A-optimality-type criterion that depends only on covariate information, requiring no response observations at the selection stage. We refer to this method as Expected Loss Optimal Selection (ELOS). By focusing on predictive risk rather than model-based optimality, ELOS remains well-defined and robust under misspecification. Simulation studies and real data applications demonstrate that ELOS achieves strong predictive performance and compares favorably with existing methods across a range of scenarios.

nominations.title: Longitudinal Brain Aging in Covariance Space: Temporally Calibrated Bayesian Inference for Adaptive Covariance Operators
nominations.authors: Montserrat Fuentes, Yi Zhao
nominations.abstract: Functional brain aging is often characterized by differences between people of different ages, although aging unfolds within individuals. This distinction is especially important for functional connectivity, where the direction of covariance change may evolve across adulthood. We introduce a Bayesian longitudinal covariance-operator framework that models each visit covariance as a latent positive-definite state informed by repeated resting-state fMRI runs. The approach calibrates run-level information for temporal dependence and replicate variability, separates within-person aging from between-person age differences, and uses an adaptive tangent representation to learn the low-dimensional structure of longitudinal change without relying on pooled covariance variation. The longitudinal operator varies smoothly in magnitude and orientation with age, while exact Fr\'echet derivatives translate the fitted trajectory to the covariance scale. This framework allows us to examine how brain covariance organization changes within individuals, whether longitudinal aging follows the population age gradient, and which functional systems contribute to their divergence. In the Dallas Lifespan Brain Study, within-person covariance aging differs substantially from the cross-sectional age gradient through early and middle adulthood, with the discrepancy diminishing later in life. Covariance reorganization is strongest around midlife, and the longitudinal signal is concentrated in a few coordinated directions, with most off-diagonal change occurring between functional systems. These findings demonstrate that population-level signatures of brain aging do not necessarily reflect individual aging trajectories and highlight the importance of modeling longitudinal covariance change directly.

nominations.title: Common Signals, Spurious Cross-Excitation, and Identification in Multivariate Hawkes Processes
nominations.authors: Jiwon Jung, Kiseop Lee
nominations.abstract: Multivariate Hawkes models are widely used to measure endogenous interactions in event data, but latent common signals can generate apparent excitation even without structural interaction. We characterize the resulting linear projection and construct stable, nonnegative Hawkes processes that share the mean intensity and Bartlett spectrum of common-signal models despite having different excitation mechanisms. This establishes a concrete form of second-order non-identification. We derive integrated third-order cumulants for Hawkes processes with Cox immigration and establish generic local identification of normalized structural parameters in two- and three-dimensional systems. An exact-equivalence Monte Carlo experiment demonstrates how third-order information can distinguish mechanisms with identical second-order structure, while revealing substantial finite-sample limitations under weak signals. For a restricted parametric family, we develop Whittle estimation from binned counts, establish consistency and asymptotic normality under appropriate identification conditions, and construct feasible sandwich standard errors accounting for estimated mean intensities. Simulations assess structural recovery and inference accuracy. An application to cryptocurrency transactions illustrates the sensitivity of inferred excitation to model specification and the limitations of structural interpretation based on spectral fit alone.

nominations.title: Model-Induced Hazard Geometry and Functional Representations in Survival Analysis
nominations.authors: Xijia Liu
nominations.abstract: Individualized survival predictions are often summarized by scalar risk scores or event probabilities at selected time horizons, although clinically relevant risk may also differ in its temporal organization. We consider finite-dimensional representations of individual hazard trajectories through interpretable hazard functionals, such as peak timing, cumulative hazard over prespecified intervals, and persistence of elevated risk. A central issue is that the richness of such representations is constrained by the hazard geometry supported by the underlying survival model. We formalize this through model-induced tangent spaces and functional ranks, derive an exact decomposition of model-supported variation into directions retained and lost by a chosen representation, and introduce a model-relative notion of local completeness. We further distinguish intrinsic model capacity from the variation actually activated by covariates. These results motivate a structured extension of AFT time scaling through a positive-affine deformation on the log-time scale, yielding a power-warp mechanism with an additional temporal deformation direction. Combined with a log-logistic reference hazard, this gives a parsimonious likelihood-based working specification for which peak timing and peak height provide complete coordinates over the unimodal regime. We also establish plug-in recovery and asymptotic inference for hazard functionals. Simulations and a lung-cancer application illustrate how model-induced restrictions propagate to hazard-functional representations.

nominations.title: Generalized Odds for Ordinal Outcomes: A Causal Inference Framework Adjusting for Covariates
nominations.authors: Runnian Huang, Dandan Shi, Lan Liu, Yunjian Yin
nominations.abstract: Background: Generalized Odds (Gen Odds) provide summaries for ordinal outcomes without requiring the proportional odds assumption. However, conventional Gen Odds compares independently drawn treatment and control outcomes and targets a population-level contrast rather than an individual-level contrast. We developed an individual-level causal formulation of Gen Odds and examined its identification. Methods: We defined the Causal Gen Odds using the joint distribution of potential outcomes and identified it under conditional independence of the potential outcomes given baseline covariates. We developed a model-based estimator using nonproportional cumulative logistic regression and introduced an odds-ratio sensitivity parameter to assess departures from conditional independence. We evaluated the estimators through simulations and illustrated them using data from the ACCORD Study. Results: In simulations, the conditional-independence estimator was approximately unbiased with 95.5% confidence interval coverage under conditional independence, but bias and undercoverage increased with residual dependence. When the sensitivity-analysis estimator incorporated the data-generating dependence parameter, bias remained below 0.01 and coverage ranged from 93.7% to 96.1% across examined settings. In the ACCORD Study, the Causal Gen Odds for right-foot pre-tibial edema was 0.909 (95% CI: 0.880 to 0.940) under conditional independence and remained stable across the examined sensitivity range. Conclusions: The Causal Gen Odds provides an individual-level estimand that complements the conventional population-level Gen Odds. This framework enables estimation of this contrast while explicitly assessing its robustness to assumptions about dependence between potential outcomes.

nominations.title: Principal Component Analysis for Zero-Inflated Probability Measures via Lorenz Curves
nominations.authors: Giacomo Aletti, Enea G. Bongiorno
nominations.abstract: This paper develops a principal component analysis framework for probability measures associated with non-negative real-valued random variables with structural zeros. Specifically, leveraging the associated Lorenz Curve (LC) and a suitable perspective transformation of the plane, a bijective embedding is defined to treat such measures as functional data in a Hilbert space. Once the random LC is embedded in this space, standard Functional Principal Component Analysis (FPCA) becomes directly applicable, and the diffeomorphic nature of the embedding allows the main convergence results and their interpretations to be transferred back to the original space of LC. The a.s. and $L^2(\mathbb{P})$ consistency of the estimated eigenfunctions, eigenvalues, and modes of variation is subsequently investigated, both in the embedded space and, by virtue of the embedding's diffeomorphism property, in the original LC space. Crucially, this consistency analysis accounts for the double stochasticity of the estimation problem: one level of randomness is tied to the underlying LC process itself, while the other stems from the empirical estimation of the LC from sample data. As a consequence, consistency of the Karhunen--Lo\`eve reconstructions is also established, guaranteeing faithful approximation of individual curves in both spaces. Finally, the proposed FPCA methodology is illustrated on a real-world dataset of global export flows and compared with a naive FPCA approach.

nominations.title: Interactive and Robust PCA Graphics with FSDA in MATLAB
nominations.authors: Marco Riani, Anthony C. Atkinson, Aldo Corbellini, Domenico Perrotta, Francesca Torti, Gianluca Morelli
nominations.abstract: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a standard method for dimension reduction and the exploratory analysis of multivariate data, but a complete applied workflow often requires more than numerical eigenvectors and static plots. This article documents a set of routines in the FSDA toolbox for MATLAB that implements an integrated workflow for interactive and robust PCA graphics. The software contribution consists of coordinating classical SVD-based PCA, dynamic biplot scaling controlled by row and column parameters, score-distance and orthogonal-distance diagnostics, hard-trimming robust PCA through the Minimum Covariance Determinant and the Forward Search, linked brushing, geographical displays, and three-dimensional projection diagnostics. The implementation returns reproducible numerical output while also exposing graphical controls for changing biplot geometry, confidence regions, displayed labels, robust trimming levels, and linked selections. The methodology is illustrated on quality-of-life indicators for Italian provinces, where the software reveals variable groups, atypical provinces, robust and non-robust PCA structures, and geographical patterns. The emphasis is on statistical software: no new PCA estimator is proposed, but established PCA and robust-PCA methodology is combined in a documented, extensible, and script-reproducible MATLAB environment.

nominations.title: Improved Forecasting for Multivariate Time Series using GNAR models with General Inverse Distance Weights
nominations.authors: Hengxu Liu, Guy P. Nason, Sourav Das, Stephen Grebby
nominations.abstract: Many multivariate time series arise on networks where relationships between variables depend on physical or more general distances. Standard vector autoregressive models struggle in such settings due to their quadratic parameter growth, while generalised network autoregressive (GNAR) models offer a parsimonious alternative by explicitly incorporating network structures. Existing GNAR formulations assume fixed weights, typically uniform or reciprocal distances, which may not reflect the true influence of distance in real systems. We introduce a novel model with general inverse distance weights (GNARID) that extends GNAR by introducing a tunable exponent parameter that controls the strength of distance penalisation. We establish theoretical results on the consistency and asymptotic normality of new GNARID estimators, including an extension to the setting where the number of nodes grows. We analyse the effect of misspecifying the exponent on forecasting error, which helps assess how much GNAR models could be improved by our tunable weights. Simulation studies confirm the theoretical properties and show measurable benefits from correct weight specification. Using the Brumadinho ground displacement dataset, we show that proper tuning of the weight exponent improves predictive performance, highlighting the practical value of flexible distance-based weighting in network time series models.

nominations.title: Testing for Peer Effects in Heteroskedastic Fixed-Effects Panels
nominations.authors: Leheng Cai, Weijia Li, Xu Guo
nominations.abstract: We study testing for peer effects in linear panel models with individual and time fixed effects when the interaction network is unspecified. We propose a quadratic-form test based on the Gram matrix of residualized peer covariates. A key difficulty is that fixed-effects removal and nuisance estimation destroy the centering of a conventional leave-diagonal-out quadratic form under conditional heteroskedasticity. We introduce a leverage adjustment that restores exact conditional centering and combine it with a residual-based variance estimator. The resulting studentized statistic is asymptotically standard normal as both panel dimensions diverge, without imposing any restriction on their relative growth rates. Under additional conditions, we establish consistency against alternatives. The null theory is further extended to covariates that are weakly dependent over time; the same studentization remains valid without an additional long-run variance estimator. Monte Carlo experiments evaluate the finite-sample size and power of the proposed test across different settings and demonstrate its favorable performance relative to the existing benchmark test. Applications to state tax competition and growth spillovers among OECD countries illustrate the practical relevance in testing for peer effects without specifying the interaction network.

nominations.title: Hierarchical Gaussian Processes for Survey Weighting: Local Equivalent Weights in Structured Populations
nominations.authors: Seonghun Lee
nominations.abstract: Regression-based survey weighting connects model-based population estimation with design-based inference through equivalent weights. For nonlinear models, equivalent weights can be defined locally through the sensitivity of a poststratified population estimator. However, conventional regression models may inadequately capture nonlinear relationships and complex interactions across sparse poststratification cells. We develop a survey-weighting framework based on hierarchical Gaussian process (HGP) regression, combining structured group-level effects with kernel-based smoothing to share information across related cells. We derive Gaussian posterior prediction formulas that exploit the structured covariance representation to reduce computational costs. We also establish a uniform convergence result for the posterior predictive mean under stated regularity conditions and construct local equivalent weights by matching the first-order sensitivity of a plug-in poststratified estimand to that of a weighted average of fitted response means, with both derivatives taken with respect to the latent mean-scale vector. Simulations show that HGP achieves lower population-weighted prediction error under nonparametric structure, whereas logistic regression performs well under correct parametric specification. Additional analyses examine sample size, frame coverage, subgroup prediction, and population-mean agreement. An application to the Future of Families and Child Wellbeing Study illustrates the method. Overall, this work extends local equivalent-weight construction to nonparametric modeling and provides a computational framework and conditional theoretical results for survey weighting in structured, sparse populations.

nominations.title: Compound p-values for competition-based testing
nominations.authors: Junu Lee, Rina Foygel Barber, Richard J. Samworth, Zhimei Ren
nominations.abstract: Standard competition-based multiple testing methods -- such as the knockoff filter and the target-decoy procedure -- are typically formulated as head-to-head competitions between a test unit and its assigned negative control unit. Motivated by real-world applications, which leverage any available negative controls, we study this competition-based framework in more intricate settings where competitions vary in size and structure. We propose new methods based on compound p-values -- p-values that are superuniform only on aggregate -- that enable powerful multiple testing with broader competition structures, via the Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg procedures. The former provides exact familywise error rate control, whereas the latter may incur a false discovery rate inflation factor, for which we derive upper bounds across a range of settings. We showcase the performance of our general competition-based testing methodology through extensive simulations and real-data applications, including analyses of virtual spatial transcriptomics and CRISPR screen datasets that exhibit precisely the complex competition structures that motivate our methods.

nominations.title: Testing Conditional Distribution Equality Using Generative Models
nominations.authors: Zekai Jin, Yi Zhang, Yun Yang, Xiaofeng Shao
nominations.abstract: Conditional distribution equality testing is a core problem with applications in causal inference, model diagnostics, and transfer learning. Existing methods often lose power when the conditioning variable is high-dimensional. We propose a new test that leverages generative models to compare conditional distributions using both observed data and synthetic samples. A sample-splitting and studentization scheme is introduced to control estimation error. Under the null, the test statistic is asymptotically normal, and we establish local power against contiguous alternatives. Our theory under the null and fixed alternative requires only consistency of the learned conditional distribution, allowing for a broad class of generative models. Empirical results demonstrate accurate size control and strong power in high-dimensional settings compared to representative kernel-based conditional and joint two-sample tests.

nominations.title: Finite-sample certification of coverage regret for budgeted document selection under adaptive stratified auditing
nominations.authors: Nora Serdyukova
nominations.abstract: Selecting a budget-constrained set of documentary fragments, for instance the knowledge base of a retrieval-augmented generation system, raises a statistical question: how much expected query coverage is lost relative to the best feasible selection when the query distribution is unknown? We construct finite-sample, distribution-free upper confidence bounds for this coverage regret that remain valid after data-dependent selection. A pilot stage may select the document set, screen competitors, build comparison networks and learn an annotation policy. Then an independent audit acquires relevance labels with probabilities that are constant within observable strata. The main result is a simultaneous bound for all retained coverage contrasts. The bound is made observable by empirical-Bernstein variance calibration or by a one-stage construction without calibration, and it accounts for estimated stratum proportions. For maximum-type coverage we prove variance contractions for swaps of redundant fragments, give a condition under which multiscale radii improve on a direct union bound, and show that such redundancy cannot be certified from samples alone. A simulation study confirms validity and quantifies the gains from variance calibration and certified redundancy.

nominations.title: Pointwise minimax lower bounds under a multi-index constraint: the price of an unknown orientation
nominations.authors: Nora Serdyukova
nominations.abstract: We consider nonparametric regression with random design and non-Gaussian noise, where the regression function has the multi-index form $F(x)=f(\Theta x)$ with an unknown link $f:\RR^m\to\RR$ in an anisotropic H\"older class and an unknown matrix $\Theta$ with $m\le d$ orthonormal rows. For estimation of $F$ at a fixed point we prove that the minimax risk is bounded from below by a multiple of $L^{1/(2\gamma+1)}(n^{-1}\ln n)^{\gamma/(2\gamma+1)}$, where $\gamma$ is the harmonic mean of the smoothness indices of the link divided by $m$. For $m<d$ this extends a Gaussian white noise result to regression. The main new case is $m=d$, where no dimension reduction takes place: the logarithmic factor still appears as soon as the link is anisotropic and the orientation of its axes is unknown. In contrast, when the link is isotropic with smoothness index at most one, the class is rotation invariant up to a constant and the classical rate without logarithm is attained. The logarithmic loss is therefore caused by the unknown orientation of the directions in which the function is least smooth

nominations.title: On Local Inference for Functionals of Ill-Posed Inverse Problems
nominations.authors: Ellen Graham, Andrea Rotnitzky
nominations.abstract: We study inference for continuous linear functionals of solutions to ill-posed inverse problems, including Euclidean parameters arising in nonparametric instrumental variables, proximal causal inference, and shadow-variable models. Although pointwise root-$n$ inference is possible under standard conditions, we show that this need not translate into locally reliable inference. Under a model imposing only minimal regularity conditions, the target is Hellinger discontinuous when both inverse problems are ill-posed: arbitrarily small changes in the data-generating law can produce arbitrarily large changes in the target, ruling out informative locally uniform inference. Imposing a uniform bound on a minimum-norm solution restores Hellinger continuity under regularity conditions, but does not by itself ensure stable root-n inference. If, in addition, both inverse problems are ill-posed and the solution whose norm is uniformly bounded is nonunique at a law $P_0$, then under regularity conditions the target fails to be pathwise differentiable; consequently, asymptotically linear estimators exhibit nonvanishing root-$n$ bias under some local alternatives, causing Wald confidence intervals to undercover asymptotically. Under regularity conditions, pathwise differentiability is restored if the uniformly bounded solution is unique at $P_0$. It is also restored, regardless of uniqueness, under the stronger requirement that the corresponding solution satisfy a uniformly bounded $\beta$-source condition for some $\beta$>0. We relate these regimes to very weak, weak, and strong identification in instrumental variables models.

nominations.title: Softplus Affine(1, 1) Processes: Enlarged Stationarity Region, Stationary Unit Roots, and Inference
nominations.authors: Yang Lu, Fukang Zhu
nominations.abstract: Softplus affine\((1,1)\) models keep the conditional mean positive while allowing coefficients of either sign. We study them under Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related conditional distributions. A stationary solution with moments of all positive orders exists whenever the coefficient sum is less than one, strictly enlarging previously known sufficient regions. At the unit root, the coefficient sum equals one. Under an invertibility condition, a stationary solution exists in this case if and only if the intercept is negative. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail with an explicit index, and the observations can exhibit long memory. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal at the usual \(\sqrt n\) rate below and at the unit root, with the coefficient sum left unrestricted in estimation. At the unit root, these results require only a finite mean and yield standard Wald inference even when the observations have infinite variance or long memory. Simulations and two applications examine finite-sample inference and sensitivity to the softplus scale.

nominations.title: A New Perspective on Cumulative Residual R\'enyi Entropy
nominations.authors: Shubham Babasaheb Alte, Swaroop Georgy Zachariah, Mohd. Arshad
nominations.abstract: This paper introduces a new cumulative residual R\'enyi entropy (CRRE), which addresses limitations of the existing cumulative residual R\'enyi entropy. The conventional measure suffers from two primary drawbacks: its failure to converge to the cumulative residual entropy (CRE) as the order parameter approaches unity, and its lack of guaranteed positivity. Our proposed CRRE resolves these issues, offering a theoretically consistent and always nonnegative measure of uncertainty in residual lifetimes. We explore its mathematical properties, including its relationship with existing information measures. Furthermore, the concept is extended to its dynamic version, and its time-dependent characteristics are investigated. A non-parametric estimator of the proposed CRRE is developed, its almost sure convergence is established, and is validated through Monte Carlo simulation. The effectiveness of CRRE as a tool for quantifying uncertainty is confirmed through its application in chaotic theory and financial data.

nominations.title: Drift parameter estimation for interacting particle systems with singular repulsion
nominations.authors: Chiara Amorino, Jacek Malecki, Radomyra Shevchenko
nominations.abstract: We study the estimation of the interaction parameter in singular interacting particle systems from continuous and discrete observations over a fixed time horizon. The singularity of the interaction drift prevents the direct application of standard likelihood and contrast-based methods, which rely on regularity assumptions that fail in this setting. Our approach exploits an exact reduction of the particle dynamics to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation for a quadratic empirical moment. By the symmetry of the interaction kernel, the singular terms cancel, yielding an explicit estimator in which the unknown parameter enters linearly. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality as the number of particles, \(N\), tends to infinity. Letting \(\varepsilon_N\) denote the microscopic noise scaling of the system, we obtain asymptotic normality at the rate \(\sqrt{N/\varepsilon_N}\) for strictly positive interaction kernels, under an additional condition on the limiting empirical information. We further extend these results to degenerate interaction kernels, achieving consistency and asymptotic normality at rate \(N\) under suitable structural assumptions and the canonical scaling \(\varepsilon_N=N^{-1}\). In both regimes, we provide conditions on the observation mesh ensuring that the statistical limits remain valid under discrete sampling, in high frequency. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of our methodology through Dyson Brownian motion, the Dyson Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, and Wishart--Laguerre particle systems, alongside a numerical investigation of the estimators' finite-sample performance.

nominations.title: Randomization Inference for Dynamic Causal Effects in Short Panels with Autoregressive Instruments
nominations.authors: Pedro Picchetti
nominations.abstract: I study randomization inference for dynamic causal effects in panels with many units and few periods when treatment is endogenous and an instrument is as good as randomly assigned only through the innovations of a first-order autoregressive assignment mechanism with unknown persistence. The persistence is a nuisance parameter in two senses: it determines which weighted average of heterogeneous causal effects the instrumented local projection estimand measures, and it governs the randomization distribution of any statistic built from the instrument. I propose tests that never estimate it. For each candidate value the innovations are recovered, rerandomized under a group that leaves their joint law invariant, and a randomization p-value is formed; the reported p-value is the supremum over candidate values or over an exact confidence set. Under a sharp null on the path of lag-specific effects the tests have level at most $\alpha$ for every persistence in finite samples, including the unit root, and the supremum is a maximum over finitely many points. Under a weak null on the heterogeneity-weighted estimand a studentized version is uniformly asymptotically valid.

nominations.title: Creative destruction: Human-AI competition in an experimental market
nominations.authors: John Conlon, Peter Schwardmann
nominations.abstract: We study two hypotheses for how a human role in production could persist despite growing AI capabilities. Humans might have a durable advantage in taste, designing better products even as AI agents automate routine tasks, or consumers might intrinsically prefer that humans have a hand in production. In our experiment, participants act as producers, designing computer games with an AI coding agent, and as consumers who buy them. Across three studies (N = 1,025), we find no evidence for either hypothesis. Games designed by an AI on its own outperform those of human producers, including both amateurs and professional creatives. Human producers do not anticipate the AI's advantage. Revealing whether a game is human-designed does not raise consumers' willingness to pay for the product.

nominations.title: Long Term Pediatric Vaccine Tender Scheduling with Quantity Discounts
nominations.authors: Nicholas Uhorchak, Ruben Proano, Sandra Eksioglu, Burak Eksioglu
nominations.abstract: Pediatric vaccine procurement for low- and lower-middle-income countries (LICs and LMICs) requires long-term coordination across heterogeneous vaccine markets, competing stakeholder objectives, and uncertain demand, yet tenders are currently scheduled as a series of independent renewals. We extend the Hypothetically Coordinated Vaccine Market (HCVM) framework to schedule multi-year tenders with flexible lengths and all-unit quantity discounts, and compare three objectives: a balanced coordinatingentity model (UG), a social-benefit model that minimizes missed doses (SB), and a producer profit-maximizing model (MP). Using UNICEF ten-year demand forecasts and 30 demand replications across six discount scenarios, we find that the procurement objective, not demand variability, drives cost-to-tender and schedule complexity. Quantity discounts favor large producers, concentrating the market and increasing supply chain vulnerability. Discount effectiveness depends on market maturity rather than valency: pentavalent and hexavalent vaccines are already near their price floor, and among monovalent vaccines only rotavirus responds to discounts, whereas HPV and PCV remain too expensive to compete. Removing pentavalent and hexavalent vaccines from the procurement pool sharply increases missed doses. These results give planners practical guidance on objective selection, discount design, and protecting access to combination vaccines.

nominations.title: Which Text Matters: Handling Model Uncertainty in Text-as-Data Regressions, with an Application to Central Bank Communication
nominations.authors: Martin Feldkircher, Bernd Prostmaier, Paul Hofmarcher, Pierre Siklos
nominations.abstract: Social scientists routinely convert text into covariates like topic shares, ideal points or sentiment scores, and insert them into statistical models of interest. This two-step design is convenient, but it is rarely guided by theory: little tells the analyst which text-based covariates to construct or include. Each approach embodies contestable measurement choices, and competing operationalizations of the same construct can support different conclusions, so a single research question gives rise to a menu of competing regression models. Which text constructed covariates belong in a model, and in what functional form, is thus a problem of model uncertainty. We propose spike-and-slab generalized additive models (SSGAMs), which jointly select covariates and determine whether their effects are linear or nonlinear. We illustrate the approach with the communication of a powerful unelected institution, asking which of 45 competing text indicators from 224 monthly European Central Bank press conferences, spanning late 2002 to mid-2025, track professional inflation expectations. A sparse set is selected; widely used alternatives, and every tested nonlinear effect, carry no incremental information.

nominations.title: An Open-Source Web-Based Viewer for Disseminating Image-Derived Models
nominations.authors: Christian Herz, Kyle Sunderland, Matthew Daemer, Julia Iacovella, Sehdev Pressley, Ashley Koluda, Csaba Pinter, Kevin Zuber, John Daniels, Allen Ladd, Mali Hetmaniuk, Kevin K. Whitehead, Andras Lasso, Matthew A. Jolley
nominations.abstract: Patient-specific 3-dimensional (3D) models are increasingly central to planning surgery and catheter-based intervention in children with congenital heart disease (CHD), whose anatomy is often atypical and variable. These models inform care only when the surgeons and interventional cardiologists who make treatment decisions can rotate, crop, and measure them directly. Desktop modeling applications require local installation, capable hardware, and training. Commercial web-based viewers are portable but closed, and, in our experience, cannot display volume rendering, time-resolved (e.g., 4-dimensional) data, or the custom workflows centers build for CHD. Because CHD populations are small and heterogeneous, such workflows are unlikely to be prioritized commercially, and end users have no means to add them. To address these limitations, we developed the SlicerHeart Viewer, an open-source module that presents a simplified interface to a complete 3D Slicer/SlicerHeart session running on a server. Clinicians access models created by clinical modeling services from any device through a web browser. Because 3D Slicer runs underneath, volume rendering, time-resolved data, and any SlicerHeart workflow, including those developed for CHD, are available without modification. The module is independent of the hosting environment; we chose internal servers behind institutional single sign-on, and a cloud-hosted option is in development. Over one year at a single pediatric center, nearly all of 82 modeled cases were shared through the Viewer with clinicians from five specialties, with cases loading in 5 to 10 seconds. The approach is not specific to CHD and is deployable at other centers.

nominations.title: Maximum likelihood, neural networks and posterior mean for inferring fractional Brownian motion parameters
nominations.authors: Daniel S. Han, Vaishnavi Ananthanarayanan, Matthew J. Simpson
nominations.abstract: Fractional Brownian motion (fBM) is a model of anomalous diffusion parameterised by a Hurst exponent $H \in (0,1)$ and a generalised diffusion coefficient $D_H > 0$. We jointly estimate $H$ and $D_H$ using maximum likelihood (MLE) from density measurements with Poisson counting noise and single-particle trajectory with Gaussian localisation error. We show that one density measurement in time cannot infer both $H$ and $D_H$ and that several time points are needed, which matters most for inference precision. For trajectories, we show that a neural network trained with a squared error loss approximates the posterior mean of $H$, which can be computed exactly at negligible cost. Paired with the profile-likelihood estimate of $D_H$, the posterior mean has the lowest root mean squared error in both $H$ and $D_H$, except near $H=0$ and $H=1$ where MLE estimates $H$ better. In vesicle trajectories from two cell types, $H$ and $D_H$ form a continuum rather than distinct modes of motion. The posterior probability that each window within a track is subdiffusive or superdiffusive shows that $26\%$ of MRC5 fibroblast and $21\%$ of HeLa vesicle trajectories contain both subdiffusive and superdiffusive windows, against $2\%$ and $7\%$ expected from estimation uncertainty alone. Intracellular cargoes therefore switch between subdiffusion and superdiffusion over time rather than forming populations with fixed $H$.

nominations.title: Distinguishing Process Change, Instrument Fault and Data-Path Corruption in Streaming Telemetry: A Reference Implementation and Benchmark
nominations.authors: Oleksandr Klymenko
nominations.abstract: A reading departs from what a monitoring system expects for one of three reasons: the physical process changed, the instrument is failing, or the value was corrupted between the instrument and the software. The three call for different responses and look alike in a single sample. We state the three-cause problem, prove which pairs of causes one channel cannot separate, and propose a bank of online detectors - a Kalman tracker with CUSUM and EWMA charts on its innovation, a Hampel median with generalized-ESD confirmation, a robust noise statistic with ADWIN, exact-value checks and an optional two-channel complementary filter - combined by a deterministic, inspectable attribution rule. The detectors were merged into a public algorithm library. On 2,942 injected events of thirteen fault types the method detects 96.3% (95% interval 95.7-97.0) at 0.22 false alarms per hour and attributes 91.2% (90.6-91.8) of detected events correctly from one channel and 99.0% (98.6-99.4) with a second, rate channel; from one channel only 2 of 207 detected sensor drifts are attributed to the instrument, as the problem statement predicts. Injected into recorded industrial signals, the same catalogue is detected at 80.8% and attributed correctly at 84.5%, at 3.6 false alarms per hour. On the Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark the method detects 32 of 33 experiments with a median delay of 15 s, at 46 false alarms per hour against 11 for a rolling z-score.

nominations.title: A Wideband STAR-RIS Employing Shared-Aperture Polarization Conversion and Diagonal Switching Topology for 6G Applications
nominations.authors: Ruiqi Wang, Atif Shamim
nominations.abstract: Simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (STAR-RIS) enable programmable wave control on both sides of a surface, extending wireless coverage beyond single-sided operation. However, practical STAR-RIS demonstrations in literature have narrow bandwidths, because it is challenging to achieve wideband reflection and transmission simultaneously from the same aperture. To overcome this limitation, a wideband STAR-RIS architecture is proposed based on shared-aperture polarization conversion and diagonal switching topology. Here, multiple resonances enable wideband magnitude responses and mirror-symmetric current reversal maintains $180^{\circ}$ phase difference in both reflection and transmission modes. Accordingly, a diagonal four-branch unit cell configuration is developed, where the tailored top patch directs the received wave either through a pair of blind vias connected by a buried strip to the shared top aperture for reflection, or to the bottom ring patch using a through via for transmission. Based on the proposed design, a 10 by 10 STAR-RIS prototype is fabricated and experimentally characterized. The measured 3-dB bandwidths reach 19.8% in reflection mode and 21.9% in transmission mode. Near-field measurements show average signal enhancements of 19.8 and 22.6 dB for reflection and transmission, respectively, over the wide frequency range of 6.8-8.4 GHz. Far-field measurements further demonstrate average received-power enhancements of 11.2 dB in reflection and 11.9 dB in transmission. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this work presents the first experimentally demonstrated wideband STAR-RIS covering the 7.125-8.4 GHz band within the emerging 6G FR3 spectrum.

nominations.title: Sequential RF Fingerprinting for AIS: Rejecting Unknown Vessels and Insider MMSI Spoofs Days After Enrollment
nominations.authors: Fawaz Abdul Razak, Bora Turgut, Mason Clark, Yasin Yilmaz
nominations.abstract: Any AIS transmitter can claim any vessel's identity (MMSI), because nothing in the protocol authenticates it; only the transmitter's analog hardware reveals who is really sending. We treat AIS traffic as streams of bursts keyed by claimed MMSI and accumulate physical-layer evidence with a sequential test. Each burst is scored by its k-nearest-neighbor distance to enrolled fingerprints in the feature space of a classifier whose weights are fixed after training, calibrated into a tail probability, and accumulated by a geometric-entropy-minimization cumulative-sum (GEM-CUSUM) statistic. The same test rejects unknown transmitters when scored against all enrolled vessels, and exposes insider spoofs when scored against the claimed vessel. A threshold refreshed from genuine traffic alone keeps it at a stated false-alarm rate as fingerprints drift. On AIS in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) recordings captured over 13 days at the Istanbul Strait (Bosphorus), the detector rejects unseen vessels at least 10 days after enrollment. Evaluated over 50-burst trials with every vessel weighted equally, it reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.956 (95% confidence interval 0.913-0.989), where the best score computed from one burst at a time reaches 0.899. A threshold refreshed from the first quarter of the enrolled vessels' traffic holds 5.3% false alarms (3.0-9.2% across five independently trained encoders) at 88.8% detection. Scored against the claimed MMSI, enrolled transmitters spoofing another vessel are rejected at 0.991, a threat that open-set tests cannot see (AUROC 0.500, chance level). The lightweight Transformer GLFormer, reimplemented from its paper (no code is public) and retrained on the same data, reaches 0.652 in the same detector with its published in-phase input and 0.849 when given the same I/Q input as our encoder.

nominations.title: Carbon-Aware Joint Resource and Energy Scheduling for Cellular Base Stations
nominations.authors: Jaebum Park, Yutao Xie, Amitava Ghosh, Yuanyuan Shi, Robert W. Heath Jr
nominations.abstract: Decarbonizing cellular networks requires coordinating communication-resource and battery operation with time-varying electricity prices and carbon intensity. We jointly optimize base station and battery operation under a carbon-adjusted electricity price and traffic-demand constraints, and solve the mixed-integer nonconvex problem through a two-stage decomposition exact under a minimum-power rule. Using California price and carbon-intensity data, we show that carbon-aware scheduling reduces emissions most when low-price and low-carbon periods are misaligned. Above a carbon price of roughly 100-300 USD/ton, battery operation shifts from cost-driven to carbon-driven, cutting emissions by up to 57.8% relative to a cost-only schedule.

nominations.title: FFDT: Sim-to-Real Domain Transfer Method for Far-Field Ground Penetrating Radar
nominations.authors: Chi Wang, Hai-Han Sun
nominations.abstract: The scarcity of real-world ground penetrating radar (RealGPR) data is a major barrier to the development of deep learning (DL) methods for GPR data processing. Although simulated GPR (SimGPR) datasets can be used to train DL models, differences in hardware configuration and system parameters between SimGPR and RealGPR create a sim-to-real domain gap that leads to poor generalization of DL models to RealGPR measurements. To address this gap, we present a physics-based far-field GPR domain transfer (FFDT) method to transfer far-field SimGPR data to the corresponding RealGPR-domain data in the same scenario. In FFDT, SimGPR and RealGPR are modeled using angle-dependent transfer functions that capture three-dimensional antenna radiation characteristics. These transfer functions are then combined with ray tracing to enable the sim-to-real data transfer. Extensive studies across diverse objects and soil conditions demonstrate that FFDT-transferred data closely match RealGPR ground truth. To further demonstrate its value for RealGPR-domain dataset generation, FFDT is implemented to build a RealGPR-domain dataset for training a DL model for clutter removal. The model achieves robust performance on RealGPR measurements. With one-time SimGPR and RealGPR system calibration, FFDT enables RealGPR-domain dataset generation without requiring task-specific RealGPR field measurements for DL model training or fine-tuning, thereby addressing the RealGPR data scarcity bottleneck and supporting reliable development and deployment of DL methods for real-world GPR applications.

nominations.title: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Integrated Sensing and Communication in IoT C-RAN
nominations.authors: Le Tung Giang, Nguyen Xuan Tung, Trinh Van Chien, Chau Yuen, Won-Joo Hwang
nominations.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with cloud radio access networks (C-RAN) unifies two foundational technologies for the Internet of Things (IoT), enabling both high-data-rate transmission and accurate environmental awareness. This paper investigates an uplink C-RAN system where multiple remote radio units (RRUs) jointly serve user equipment devices (UEs) and sense a target. We demonstrate that only a subset of RRUs is typically needed to meet sensing requirements, while energy is potentially conserved by deactivating redundant sensing RRUs. Motivated by this, we aim to improve the system's energy efficiency (EE) by jointly optimizing RRU activation, user association, and power allocation, while ensuring localization accuracy through the Cram\'er-Rao lower bound (CRLB). To address this problem, we propose a model-based iterative algorithm that integrates optimal user association, decision tree-based selection of sensing RRUs, and fixed-point power allocation. This algorithm is further used to train a graph neural network (GNN) framework, ISAC-GNN, to overcome scalability and computational complexity limitations. Our theoretical analysis ensures performance guarantees, while a semi-supervised training strategy enhances stability and generalization. Simulation results demonstrate that ISAC-GNN reduces inference time by 67% relative to the model-based approach, enabling real-time implementation for ISAC system resource management. In addition, ISAC-GNN allows scalable deployment across various system scenarios without retraining the model.

nominations.title: Hardware-friendly Baseband Design and Performance Analysis for LEO Broadband LoS-MIMO Systems
nominations.authors: Peixin Zhang, Fengkui Gong, Guo Li, Tony Q. S. Quek
nominations.abstract: High-frequency and broadband line-of-sight multiple-input multiple-output (LoS-MIMO) is a key solution for massive space-to-Earth data downlinks. However, in low Earth orbit (LEO) scenarios, it faces spatial rank deficiency from time-frequency coupling correlation and clock deviations from distributed oscillators. This paper establishes a dynamic effective channel throughput (ECT) framework incorporating waterfall characteristics of forward error correction. A hardware-friendly OFDM-based transceiver architecture with subband-adaptive truncation and dynamic timing recovery to achieve robust spatial decoupling is proposed. Through rigorous closed-form derivations, the equivalent signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) under joint errors is quantified, and an optimal scheduling algorithm combining truncation with variable coding and modulation is proposed to maximize ECT. Simulations confirm that the design circumvents outages caused by spatial notches with low complexity, stably enhancing the potential average throughput of a single dual-polarized beam to over 100 Gbps, providing a reliable theoretical foundation and baseband solution for next-generation high-throughput satellites.

nominations.title: Simultaneous Secure Communications and Sensing Privacy with Full Duplex MIMO Radios
nominations.authors: Ioannis Gavras, George C. Alexandropoulos
nominations.abstract: This paper proposes a Full Duplex (FD) framework for safeguarding Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) against a passive multi-antenna Eavesdropper (Eve). The adversary is modeled as both a communication and sensing threat, seeking to decode uplink data streams and estimate the surrounding scene. Eve's threat is quantified through two worst-case requirements over a location uncertainty region: a minimum secrecy rate for data confidentiality and a minimum eavesdropping Cramer-Rao Bound (CRB) for sensing privacy. We derive the eavesdropping information measures governing both data interception and scene inference, showcasing that transmitting Artificial Noise (AN) can degrade Eve's capabilities through the inverse interference-plus-noise covariance. Exploiting the underlying structure of the problem, we characterize finite-power local and robust feasibility conditions for target secrecy-privacy pairs. The analysis showcases that AN is fundamentally subspace-limited: increasing power is beneficial only along Eve's communication channel and sensing-derivative directions illuminated by the effective AN subspace. Finally, we formulate an AN power allocation problem that is solved via monotone branch-and-bound, and numerical evaluations quantify the AN power required to guarantee joint secrecy and sensing privacy.

nominations.title: Comparative Analysis and Behavioral Modelling of Power Amplifiers in FR3
nominations.authors: Cel Thys, Rodney Martinez Alonso, Ali H Alsarraf, Zhuangzhuang Cui, Dominique Schreurs, Sofie Pollin
nominations.abstract: Power amplifier (PA) nonlinearity is a critical transmitter impairment in the upper mid-band (7 GHz to 24 GHz), designated as Frequency Range 3 (FR3) in emerging 6G standardisation. The 3GPP PA model baseline, TR 38.803 Annex A, was derived from 2.1 GHz and 28 GHz measurements and has not been revisited yet for FR3 standards work. This paper addresses that gap with characterisation measurements of multiple PA devices-under-test (DUTs), driven into gain compression in the 7 GHz and 15 GHz bands with 100 MHz and 200 MHz bandwidth. Memoryless polynomial and Generalized Memory Polynomial (GMP) behavioral models are extracted by least-squares regression and compared with 3GPP models spanning FR1 and FR2. The GaN PA DUT is modelled best at a higher nonlinear order and shows markedly stronger phase distortion than the wideband PA. The memory terms of the GMP model measurably improve the Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) at all operating points. An orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) ambiguity function analysis from the Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) literature, using the extracted models, illustrates how PA compression raises the sidelobe floor of the sensing response. These results provide a reference for PA impairment modelling in FR3, directly applicable to ISAC system design. All model coefficients and measurement data are publicly available [1].

nominations.title: DeepPV-MRF: End-to-End Partial-Volume Fraction Estimation from MR Fingerprinting Time Series
nominations.authors: Tianyi Ding, Yang Gao, Zhuang Xiong, Feng Liu, Martijn A. Cloos, Jin Jin, Hongfu Sun
nominations.abstract: Background: Estimating subvoxel tissue fractions from magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is challenging. Conventional dictionary matching and segmentation pipelines can propagate errors from intermediate parametric maps into tissue fraction estimates. Purpose: We introduce DeepPV-MRF, a deep learning framework that directly estimates voxel-wise tissue fractions from raw MRF signals. Methods: A cascaded spatial-temporal network was trained on subject-derived Bloch simulations with radial k-space undersampling. The network combines temporal encoding and spatial U-Net refinement to estimate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), gray matter (GM), and white matter (WM) fractions without intermediate T1/T2 maps. We compared DeepPV-MRF with partial-volume dictionary matching (PV-DM) and pseudoinverse estimation (PV-Pinv) using simulated and in vivo data. Results: DeepPV-MRF outperformed both methods across acquisition settings. In single-shot simulations, CSF/WM/GM mean absolute errors were 0.0418/0.0744/0.0757, versus 0.1281/0.2443/0.2958 for PV-DM and 0.2021/0.2793/0.2630 for PV-Pinv. Corresponding structural similarity values were 0.960/0.916/0.922. In vivo results showed sharper anatomical boundaries and smoother tissue transitions, while cross-shot analysis indicated improved consistency across volunteers. Conclusions: DeepPV-MRF enables accurate and efficient direct tissue fraction estimation from MRF signals, particularly with limited shots. Further validation is needed before clinical deployment.

nominations.title: Toward Motion Capture Textiles: A Batteryless IMU Array Powered and Networked Through a Conductive-Fabric Bus
nominations.authors: Ryusei Miyakawa, Akihito Noda
nominations.abstract: Motion capture is increasingly important in healthcare, rehabilitation, and sports applications. However, conventional vision-based systems require camera infrastructure and line-of-sight conditions, limiting their use in daily environments. This paper proposes a location-independent platform for motion capture, based on an array of IMU (inertial measurement unit) sensor nodes without individual wiring or onboard batteries, enabled by two-dimensional communication and power delivery over conductive fabric. Pipeline processing in each sensor node, combined with a token-passing protocol, enables collision-free and stable data acquisition at 50 Hz. Real-time three-dimensional reconstruction of flexible objects is further demonstrated by applying Hermite spline interpolation to orientation data from grid-aligned IMUs. Against a cylinder of known radius, the reconstructed surface deviates by 2.60 mm RMS over the 225 mm span of the array. The reconstruction is formulated for the quasi-static regime, and this letter empirically validates it in that regime. The hardware platform and communication protocol implemented in this work enable further investigation toward dynamic motion capture textiles.

nominations.title: Hybrid Monostatic and Bistatic Sensing for Target Localization in OFDM Systems under Phase Noise
nominations.authors: Luc\'ia Pallar\'es Rodr\'iguez, Musa Furkan Keskin, Alireza Pourafzal, Jos\'e A. L\'opez-Salcedo, Gonzalo Seco-Granados, Henk Wymeersch
nominations.abstract: In hybrid monostatic-bistatic orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) sensing, each sensing node receives a superposition of monostatic and bistatic target returns, whose phase-noise (PN) characteristics differ fundamentally due to oscillator sharing. While monostatic sensing benefits from partial PN cancellation through the common transmit-receive oscillator, bistatic sensing involves independent oscillators and is therefore more strongly affected by PN. In this paper, we characterize the joint residual differential PN statistics of these superimposed components in a centralized two-node sensing system and quantify their impact on target localization via theoretical lower bounds considering three different receivers: (i) PN-free ideal receiver, (ii) PN-aware receiver that exploits the joint PN statistics, and (iii) PN-ignorant receiver that neglects PN.

nominations.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
nominations.authors: Craig Jin, Thomas Chaffey
nominations.abstract: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. Transistor-level SKY130 simulations show that the second run gives the gradient within 1.9%; that hardware linearisation permits large, noise-robust error signals; that a 13-cell network learns the Iris data set; and that learning in situ restores mismatched circuits on which software-trained weights fail, from 53-63% to 88-96% test accuracy.

nominations.title: Sampling Reduction for Near-Field to Far-Field Transformation of Bistatic Radar Target Measurements
nominations.authors: Getahun Kibret Tadesse, Thomas Dallmann
nominations.abstract: Accurate bistatic radar cross-section (RCS) characterization requires near-field measurements over multiple dimensions, which, under typical near-field sampling requirements, can lead to long measurement durations for electrically large radar targets. This paper presents a near-field-to-far-field transformation based on an equivalent surface-current reconstruction using a-priori information about the target to reduce the number of newly acquired near-field samples. It is assumed that the prior target and the target under test (TUT) differ by localized geometrical modifications. Their complex differential near field is reconstructed using Tikhonov-regularized least squares QR factorization (LSQR) method. The reconstructed differential far- field contribution is coherently combined with the prior far-field contribution to estimate the bi-static RCS of the TUT. The method is preliminarily evaluated using simulations of a complex target at 6 GHz. The results indicate that, for the investigated simulation case, prior information can be used to thin out the sampling grid by 90% while maintaining close agreement with the simulation baseline.

nominations.title: Radial-Angular Resolution Framework for Near-Field Communications
nominations.authors: Viviana Centritto, Sotiris Droulias, Angeliki Alexiou
nominations.abstract: Near-field beamfocusing confines radiated power into a localized three-dimensional focal spot, making the analytical characterization of radial and angular resolution critical for sixth-generation (6G) multi-user systems, yet existing models treat the focal resolution as a fixed geometric outcome rather than a tunable design variable. Based on the Angular Representation (ASR) approach, this paper presents a resolution framework to design contiguous focal regions across both the radial and angular domain for steered multi-user systems. By extending the definition of a tunable inter-beam overlap $\rho$, we derive closed-form expressions for the radial and angular focal boundaries and extents, alongside the steering-dependent minimum focal distance $d_{0,\text{min}}$ and maximum steering angle $\theta_{\text{max}}$. Using these boundaries, iterative synthesis algorithms are developed to construct uniform and non-uniform radial and angular beam arrangements. Finally, by analyzing both isolated and joint radial-angular configurations, we quantify the fundamental trade-offs between $\rho$, achievable user capacity, inter-user interference, and system sum-rate across varying steering angles.

nominations.title: Movable-Antenna Relay Enhanced Multiuser Communications: Reinforcement Learning-Based Antenna Positioning and Power Allocation
nominations.authors: Yuanjun Zhang, Lipeng Zhu, Haobin Mao, Zhe Li, Zhenyu Xiao
nominations.abstract: Movable antenna (MA) has emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communication performance by flexibly reconfiguring wireless channels via antenna movement. In this paper, we propose an MA relay-enhanced multiuser communication system that adopts a half-duplex decode-and-forward (DF) relay scheme. The relay node is equipped with an MA array, and a buffer is employed to enhance the end-to-end transmission performance. Specifically, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the minimum average achievable rate among multiple users over a given transmission period by dynamically optimizing the positions of MAs, transmit power, and beamforming matrices, subject to the constraints on antenna movement, inter-antenna spacing, and total energy budget for antenna movement and transmission. To address this non-convex problem with highly coupled variables, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based algorithm, where a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm is utilized to optimize the antenna positions and power allocation, while the transmit and receive beamforming solutions are obtained through closed-form expressions in each time slot. Numerical results validate the efficacy of the proposed RL-based algorithm and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed MA relay-enhanced multiuser communication system over the conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA)-based relay system and other MA-based benchmarks.

nominations.title: Radar-Only Long-Term Beam Prediction in mmWave Vehicular Networks: An Empirical Study of Doppler Input and Cross-Modal Distillation
nominations.authors: Jeongwan Kang, Miguel Bordallo L\'{o}pez, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Junhyeong Kim, Sunwoo Kim
nominations.abstract: Sensing-aided beam prediction could cut the beam-training overhead of millimeter-wave vehicular links, and two design choices could strengthen a radar-only predictor: a Doppler-resolved input and knowledge distilled from a camera during training. We measure what each is worth in received power rather than in top-1 accuracy, whose differences of a few points amount to only tenths of a decibel. We use real DeepSense 6G measurements, mainly at one roadside site, and one convolutional-recurrent predictor family evaluated open-loop up to 0.67 s ahead. Adding a range-Doppler map to the range-angle map lowers the mean beam-selection loss by 0.28 dB (95% bootstrap interval [0.14, 0.41]). The gain comes from the Doppler content, not from the extra input, and replicates, as pre-specified, at a second base station, although holding the last measured beam beats both predictors there. Cross-modal knowledge distillation from a motion-mask vision-radar teacher, by contrast, changes received power by -0.01 dB ([-0.07, +0.06]). The tested teacher, student, fusion and distillation variants show the same null in the metric each was scored on. Where distillation helps, in an exploratory run with few training passes, a radar-only teacher trained on all training passes reproduces most of the gain. For this predictor family and the full training set, the measurable gain at the link comes from Doppler-resolved radar content; no tested route for transferring training-only visual information adds a resolved gain.

nominations.title: Sensing-Aided Vehicular Beam Tracking: System Gain Over Link Feedback and Probe-Verified Sensing Invocation
nominations.authors: Jeongwan Kang, Miguel Bordallo L\'{o}pez, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Junhyeong Kim, Sunwoo Kim
nominations.abstract: Sensor-based beam prediction is usually evaluated against exhaustive beam training, leaving open when sensing adds useful information beyond a deployed tracker's link feedback and when it should be withheld. We separate system gain from the marginal value of sensing in action-restricted causal replay of recorded 64-beam sweeps from four vehicular DeepSense 6G scenarios. The replay exposes only serving-beam and explicitly probed candidate powers and counts probes and model invocations separately. The proposed controller combines a scheduled post-setup re-sweep with probe-verified sensing admission and blacklist backoff. In three scenarios where feedback-only tracking is within 0.25 dB of the recorded-sweep oracle, the controller stays close to feedback-only in mean loss while rarely invoking the model, whereas always-on sensing performs worse. In the sole high-innovation scenario, the controller's system gain is 0.82 dB (95% confidence interval [0.30, 1.40]) over the plain feedback-only tracker and 0.15 dB over a probe-limited re-sweeping reference, with fewer probes than either. Sensing and the re-sweep both correct setup lock loss. At the native decision interval, enabling sensing in the same controller yields no statistically resolved loss reduction but cuts probing by 21%. In this scenario, accurate sensing reduces loss relative to the sensor-disabled controller under emulated link noise, staleness or longer decision intervals. Weak or delayed sensing can instead increase loss despite probe verification. These exploratory results characterize sensing as a conditional substitute for RF probing or a source of loss reduction, depending on the limitations of link feedback and on the accuracy and timeliness of sensing.

nominations.title: TRP-UE Bistatic Sensing for 6G Performance Analysis and Insights
nominations.authors: Necati Kagan Erkek, Marco Di Renzo, Arman Shojaeifard, Yasser Mestrah, Remun Koirala, Mohammad Heggo, Kunjan Shah
nominations.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) equips cellular networks with the dual capability of data transmission and environmental sensing by sharing spectrum, waveforms, and radio hardware. While network-side sensing via transmission-reception points (TRPs) has been widely investigated, the use of user equipment (UEs) as sensing receivers introduces additional bistatic viewpoints and can improve target observability. UE-assisted operation is nevertheless constrained by small UE apertures and by waveform processing, especially when data-bearing communication signals are reused for sensing. The present paper investigates theoretical limits and operating conditions for UE-assisted passive target positioning, with emphasis on hybrid operation that fuses TRP--TRP and TRP--UE measurements. A unified OFDM-based signal-and-noise model is developed to cover both positioning reference signals (PRS) and communication waveform reuse with modulation-dependent noise enhancement. Based on this model, closed-form Fisher-information expressions and Cramer-Rao lower bounds are derived for delay and angular parameters and are mapped to positioning error bounds (PEBs) for two estimator classes: time-angle positioning based on TDOA + DoA and delay-only 3D ellipsoid positioning based on excess-delay/TDOA measurements. Monte-Carlo simulations across reference SNR, subcarrier spacing and occupied bandwidth, modulation order, radar cross section (RCS), sensing mode, and positioning algorithm identify regimes where UE participation and hybrid sensing provide significant gains and quantify the associated estimator-to-bound trade-offs.

nominations.title: FlowSep-RF: Rectified Flow Matching for Single-Channel Radio-Frequency Signal Separation
nominations.authors: Mohamed Kamel, Tamer Nadeem
nominations.abstract: Single-channel radio-frequency (RF) signal separation is important for interference mitigation when a signal of interest overlaps with a co-channel interferer in time and frequency. Classical matched filtering and LMMSE receivers are limited under structured non-Gaussian interference, while diffusion and score-based methods often require iterative sampling or optimization. We propose FlowSep-RF, a rectified flow matching framework that learns a clean-endpoint transport from the received mixture to the signal of interest. The model combines time-domain IQ samples with frequency-domain features and recovers the separated waveform using one endpoint velocity evaluation. We evaluate FlowSep-RF on QPSK mixtures with OFDM-BPSK, OFDM-QPSK, and RFChallenge CommSignal2 interference against classical, discriminative, and generative baselines. FlowSep-RF achieves the lowest average BER and MSE among evaluated baselines across all three settings with one-step inference.

nominations.title: Invertible subalgebras for chiral semion topological order
nominations.authors: Yu-An Chen, Meng Sun, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Zongyuan Wang, Bowen Yang
nominations.abstract: Chiral topological order is incompatible with strictly two-dimensional local commuting-projector Hamiltonians on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Invertible subalgebras (ISAs) provide an alternative framework. We construct an ISA supporting chiral semions, together with its anti-semion commutant, on a square lattice with one qubit per edge.
